A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose to learn a binary tree of value functions in an augmented MDP, which can be combined with discrete-action reinforcement learning algorithms to solve problems with multidimensional and continuous actions.

we have developed a new algorithm to learn and act in domains with multidirectional and/or continuous control, which is based on an efficient action selection mechanism embedded in the learning algorithm.

we present an approach for reinforcement learning with multidimensional continuous control variables that is computationally efficient, and can be used with any discrete action reinforcement learning algorithm for policy learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
efficient action selection can be integrated into reinforcement learning algorithms in a principled way, without requiring changes to their learning mechanisms.
efficient action selection is not only possible but also can be embedded into the learning process in a principled manner.

the problem of efficient action selection can be embedded in the learning algorithm and the resulting approach is not only computationally tractable, but also effective in learning policies for multidimensional continuous action problems.
